title: Java Read Files
learningObjectives: Read text with Files.readString and a Path.
Use BufferedReader to process a file line by line.
Handle missing files and other IOExceptions.

understand.concept: Java provides several ways to read text files. Files.readString is convenient for small files, Files.readAllLines returns all lines as a list, and BufferedReader supports line-by-line processing without loading the entire file at once. Text must be decoded using the correct character set; UTF-8 is a common explicit choice. Reading can fail, for example when a file is missing or access is denied, so handle IOException.
understand.whyItMatters: Reading files turns stored information into data that a program can process. Choosing between whole-file and streaming APIs helps control memory use, while explicit decoding and clear exception handling make file input more reliable.
understand.analogy: Think of a path as a labeled address to a storage location; the address and the data stored there are different things.
understand.analogyLimit: A path is not a guarantee that the target exists or that the program has permission to access it.

explain.narrative:
## Choose a reading strategy

The `java.nio.file.Files` class provides convenient text-reading methods. `Files.readString(path, charset)` is suitable for small files that comfortably fit in memory. `Files.readAllLines(path, charset)` returns all lines as a List and also loads the complete file. Neither is the best choice for an arbitrarily large file.

## Process large files line by line

Use `Files.newBufferedReader(path, charset)` with try-with-resources when a file should be processed incrementally. Call `readLine()` repeatedly until it returns `null`, which signals end-of-file. This avoids storing every line in a List, although the program still holds the current line and any data it chooses to accumulate.

## Decode text with the correct charset

Text files contain bytes. A reader decodes those bytes into characters using a charset. If the file is UTF-8, specify `StandardCharsets.UTF_8` when reading. Using a different charset can produce incorrect characters even when the file itself is intact.

## Handle input failures

A read can fail because the path is missing, the target is a directory, permission is denied or an I/O error occurs. Handle `IOException` at a useful application boundary and show a meaningful message. Do not treat an empty file and a missing file as the same condition.

## Common mistakes

- Calling readAllLines for a file that may be too large for memory.
- Forgetting to close a BufferedReader.
- Assuming readLine returns an empty string at end-of-file; it returns `null`.
- Using a different charset from the one used to encode the file.
- Catching an exception and continuing with data that was never read.

examples.title: Read an entire file
examples.explanation: readString loads the text of a small file into one String.

examples.title: Read all lines
examples.explanation: readAllLines returns a list containing each line from the file.

examples.title: Read line by line
examples.explanation: BufferedReader reads one line at a time and returns null when the end is reached.

examples.title: Read with UTF-8
examples.explanation: Using the same explicit charset for writing and reading avoids platform-default ambiguity.

examples.title: Count characters
examples.explanation: String.length reports the number of UTF-16 code units in the decoded text.

practise.guidedTask: Create a UTF-8 text file containing three product names. Read it once with Files.readString and once with Files.newBufferedReader. Print each line and count the number of lines. Close the reader with try-with-resources and explain why readLine returning null ends the loop.
practise.independentTask: Build a small text-file summary tool. It must report a missing input file clearly, read a small file line by line, count non-empty lines and avoid loading the entire file into a List. Include an empty-file test, a three-line test and an I/O failure discussion.
hints: Use Files.readString only when the entire file is suitably small; use BufferedReader for incremental line processing.
readLine returns null at end-of-file; an empty line is an empty String, not null.
Specify the same charset used to encode the file, commonly StandardCharsets.UTF_8, and close the reader with try-with-resources.
practise.challenge: Compare readString, readAllLines and BufferedReader for a very large log file. Explain memory behaviour, resource ownership, decoding and how you would report a missing or unreadable file without confusing it with an empty file.

questions.prompt: Which method reads a small text file into one String?
questions.explanation: readString() reads the file contents as a String (with an explicit charset overload).

questions.prompt: What does readLine return at end of file?
questions.explanation: A missing or absent parent path is represented as null by the relevant File parent accessor.

questions.prompt: Which method returns all file lines as a List?
questions.explanation: readAllLines() reads text into a list of lines.

questions.answer: To make text decoding explicit and consistent
options: To make text decoding explicit and consistent
questions.explanation: Specifying a charset makes decoding predictable across machines.

questions.prompt: Which approach suits processing a large text file line by line?
questions.explanation: BufferedReader provides efficient line-oriented character input.
